workflows.name: Monitor EU EUDAMED recalls and MDR certificates with Apify, OpenAI and Slack

user.name: Francesco Pacifico
user.bio: Software engineer building HTTP-first Apify Actors & ready-to-run n8n automation pipelines for SecOps/TPRM vendor risk, KYB compliance, public procurement, EU healthcare, and judicial auctions.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to monitor tracked EU EUDAMED UDI-DIs and manufacturer SRNs via Apify, keeps a stateful audit log in an n8n Data Table and Google Sheets, uses OpenAI to triage urgent compliance changes into CAPA guidance, and posts a consolidated alert brief to Slack.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule (or manually in sample mode) and ensures the n8n Data Table used to store EUDAMED regulatory state exists.
Pulls device and expiring MDR certificate data from the Apify “EU EUDAMED Intelligence” actor based on your UDI-DI and SRN watchlists (or generates built-in sample records for testing).
Compares the latest Apify results with the stored state to detect new entities, recalls/FSCAs, conformity or risk changes, and certificate expiry countdown updates, then upserts the current state to the n8n Data Table.
Appends the detected changes to a Google Sheets tab as an audit ledger.
Selects only items that are new, changed, or due for an expiry reminder and sends up to five of the highest-priority items to OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini) to generate structured MDR/IVDR urgency, article references, impact summaries, and recommended QA actions.
Emails urgent items to a QA/RA address via Gmail and posts a grouped, consolidated regulatory brief to a Slack channel.
After Slack accepts the message, stamps the corresponding entities in the Data Table as notified/reminded, and if Apify or Slack fails it triggers an error workflow to post a failure alert to Slack.

Setup
Create an Apify token in Apify and add an n8n HTTP Header Auth credential that sets Authorization: Bearer , then select it in both Apify HTTP Request steps.
Add credentials for OpenAI, Google Sheets, Gmail, and Slack, and set the Slack channel where the brief and failure alerts should be posted.
Set your Google Sheets document ID and ensure a sheet/tab named EUDAMED_Audit exists for appending the audit log.
Update the watchlist and policy values (UDI-DIs, SRNs, expiry window, reminder days, QA email, and max items) in the configuration step, and optionally test using sampleDay 1 then sampleDay 2 before enabling live Apify calls.
In n8n workflow settings, set this workflow (or a dedicated one) as the error workflow so failures generate the Slack failure alert.

Requirements
n8n 2.48+ with Data Tables enabled (Cloud or self-hosted, core nodes only)
Apify account + API token (francescopacifico1905/eudamed-intelligence Pay-Per-Event)
OpenAI API key, Google Sheets, Gmail, and Slack workspace access

Customization
Adjust remindDaysBefore (90,30,7) or expiringWithinDays in Set UDI-DI Watchlist, SRNs & Alert Policy.
Customize CAPA scoring criteria in AI MDR/IVDR CAPA Triage or raise maxTotalChargeUsd on the Apify nodes for large hospital SKU catalogs.

Additional info
Uses synchronous Pay-Per-Event Apify calls capped at $0.25 per HTTP step; retry-on-fail is intentionally disabled to prevent double billing. Diagnostic NOT_FOUND / INVALID_IDENTIFIER items are never billed by the Actor.

workflows.name: Guard workflows and log incidents with the n8n API, data tables and email
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow provides an n8n “safety net” by logging failed workflow executions to an n8n Data Table and sending email alerts, and by fingerprinting workflows nightly or via a secured webhook using the n8n API to detect suspicious edits and store clean versions.

How it works
Triggers when another workflow errors (as an n8n error workflow), on a nightly schedule, or via a Header Auth–protected webhook for before/after edit checks.
Routes the incoming event to either the incident-handling path or the workflow snapshot/guard path based on the payload.
For incidents, extracts key failure details (workflow, execution ID, failed node, error message, and execution URL) and inserts them into an n8n Data Table as a dead-letter log.
Sends an SMTP email alert with the incident details even if the Data Table insert fails.
For snapshots, uses the n8n API to fetch workflows and computes a content-based fingerprint (hash, node count, non-ASCII counts, U+FFFD replacement characters, and question marks).
Compares the current fingerprints to the latest stored fingerprints in an n8n Data Table, stores a new workflow version and updates the latest fingerprint when changes are safe, and flags warnings/errors for suspicious changes.
Emails a report when warnings or errors are detected, and for webhook-driven checks responds with JSON and an HTTP 409 status on errors so calling scripts can stop a deployment.

Setup
Create three n8n Data Tables named workflow_incidents, workflow_versions, and workflow_fingerprints with the columns expected by the insert/upsert steps.
Add credentials for n8n API (to read workflows), SMTP (to send alerts), and Header Auth (to protect the webhook endpoint).
Update the recipient and sender addresses in the workflow settings values (alertTo and alertFrom).
Activate (publish) this workflow so the nightly schedule and the webhook run, then set it as the "Error workflow" in the settings of each workflow you want to protect.
For API-based edits, call the webhook with {"action":"before"|"after","workflowId":""} and ensure your script stops if the response status is 409.

Requirements
n8n with data tables. Tested on n8n 2.47.7 (self-hosted).

workflows.name: Track outperforming YouTube competitor videos with Apify, Claude and Telegram

user.name: Sedge Labs
user.bio: Sedge Labs is an AI engineering studio in Dubai. We design and build AI agents and automations, in n8n or custom code, where a person approves the steps that matter. For a workflow built around your process, write to hello@sedgelabs.dev.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Checks your competitor YouTube channels every week with Apify and remembers view counts in a Data Table. Flags new outlier videos and older videos that are speeding up, reads the comments on them, has Claude explain why they worked, and sends a digest to Telegram.

How it works
A weekly schedule (Monday 08:00, your n8n instance's timezone) or a manual run starts the Settings node, which holds every value you can change.
A Data Table node creates the memory table on the first run and reads every saved video.
One request to the Apify actor sedgelabs/youtube-channel-scraper gets the latest videos of all channels with exact view counts and publish dates. If this call fails, a short failure notice goes to the delivery step and nothing is saved.
A Code node takes each channel's median views and flags two kinds of video. A new outlier was published within recentDays and has at least outlierMultiple times the median views. A climbing video is older than that window, and its views gained per day since the saved snapshot are at least outlierMultiple times the median daily gain of the channel's other older videos (it needs 3 of them, and it is not flagged again for 4 weeks). The gain must also be at least minClimbPercent percent of the channel's median views per day (0.5 by default), so an old video that gains a few dozen views is not flagged. A video seen for the first time has no gain. A snapshot younger than minHoursBetweenSnapshots is kept as the baseline, so a quick rerun does not erase it.
If anything is flagged, a second Apify request (sedgelabs/youtube-comments-scraper) gets the top comments on those videos, and a Code node picks up to 8 per video: the most liked and the ones that read as questions or requests.
If useClaude is true, Claude writes why each video likely worked (from its title and numbers) and what viewers ask for next (from the picked comments), then one video idea to test. If Claude is off or fails, the digest lists the picked comments instead.
A Code node builds a plain-text digest under 3,500 characters. A week with nothing flagged still gets a short digest with the top gainers.
With deliverTo set to telegram, the digest is sent first. Then every fetched video is saved to the Data Table, and the videos that were in the digest get a reported date. If delivery fails, nothing is saved. With none, the digest is the workflow output.

Setup
Create an Apify account, copy your API token, and add an n8n Header Auth credential with Name Authorization and Value Bearer . Select it on both Apify HTTP Request nodes.
Add an Anthropic credential with your Claude API key and select it on the Ask Claude node.
Open the Settings node and list your competitors in channels (handles, URLs or channel IDs, separated by commas). Change outlierMultiple, recentDays, maxVideosPerChannel, maxVideosInDigest or claudeModel if you want.
To get the digest in Telegram, create a bot with BotFather, add a Telegram credential, select it on the Send digest on Telegram node, and set deliverTo to telegram and telegramChatId in Settings. n8n will not publish a workflow whose Telegram node has no credential, so if you only use none, delete that node and the Send to Telegram? node and connect Build digest to Prepare rows to save.
Execute the workflow once. The first run saves a baseline and reports new outliers only. Daily gains show from the next run that is at least minHoursBetweenSnapshots later. Publish the workflow to run it every Monday.

Requirements
n8n 2.3.0 or later. The Data Table node's table Create operation, which the first run uses, arrived in 2.3.0. Built and tested on n8n 2.45.1.
An Apify account with an API token, and an Anthropic API key (skip it by setting useClaude to false).
A Telegram bot token and chat ID only if deliverTo is telegram.
Apify prices: $0.001 per video row plus $0.001 per exact-details row, so 3 channels at 20 videos each is at most $0.12 a run. The comments actor charges $1.00 per 1,000 comments plus $0.002 per video, so 5 flagged videos at 80 comments each is at most $0.41. A test run on three channels came to about $0.48 at these prices. Claude's cost for the one note is not included.

Customization
Replace the Telegram node with a Slack or Send Email node and use {{ $json.digest }} as the message. Keep it between Send to Telegram? and Prepare rows to save so rows are still saved only after delivery.
Change the Weekly schedule node to another day. Set recentDays to match the gap between runs.
Lower outlierMultiple to flag more videos, or raise it to flag fewer.
Use another tableName per client, or per niche, to keep separate memories.
Give each memory table a name that is not the start of another table's name in the same project. In n8n 2.45.1 the Create table step can fail with "already exists" while a second table with the same name plus "2" exists.
Raise minClimbPercent if older videos are flagged on gains too small to matter, or set it to 0 to turn the floor off.
Rows without an exact view count are left out of the medians and are not saved.

Additional info
By Sedge Labs (sedgelabs.dev). Actors: YouTube Channel Scraper (https://apify.com/sedgelabs/youtube-channel-scraper) and YouTube Comments Scraper (https://apify.com/sedgelabs/youtube-comments-scraper).

workflows.name: Track EU tender deadline changes and send briefs with Apify and Slack

user.name: Kizuki
user.bio:
Public data as clean rows. Pay per returned row; failed rows are not charged. Custom work: kizukidata.com/custom
Apify Actors for EU tenders, YouTube transcripts, company contacts, Google Maps, ads and more: apify.com/kizukidata

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to fetch new and changed EU tender notices from the Apify EU Tenders Scraper (TED), maintains one tracked row per procedure in an n8n Data Table, and posts a single Slack morning brief highlighting changed deadlines/cancellations, due-soon reminders, and new tenders.

How it works
Runs every day at 07:00 (or manually in a sample mode) and loads the configured filters and brief settings.
Pulls only new TED notices from the Apify EU Tenders Scraper (TED) Actor (or generates sample notices for a test run).
Merges the returned notices into an n8n Data Table keyed by procedure, updating existing rows for change notices and creating rows for newly discovered procedures.
Reads all tracked procedures and compiles a Slack-ready brief with three sections: Changed (including old vs. new deadlines and cancellations), Due soon (based on reminder day thresholds), and New.
Posts the brief to a Slack channel, splitting into multiple messages if needed to stay within Slack message length limits.
After Slack accepts each message, updates the corresponding Data Table rows to stamp which tenders were notified/changed/reminded so they are not reposted.
If the Apify search fails, hits the maxItems cap, or Slack rejects a message, stops the run so an Error Trigger posts a failure alert to Slack.

Setup
Install the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify and add an Apify API token credential.
Add a Slack OAuth2 credential with chat:write, set the target channel in both Slack steps (brief and failure alert), and invite the Slack app to that channel.
Review and update the values in “Your settings” (countries, CPV codes, keywords, publishedWithinDays, maxItems, timezone, remindDaysBefore, and changeAlerts).
Ensure the workflow can create and access the n8n Data Table named eu_tender_procedures (it is created automatically on first run).
In n8n Workflow Settings, set the correct timezone and select this workflow as its own Error Workflow so the failure alert runs on errors.
(Optional) Run “Try it with sample notices” and change sampleDay to 2 to test change/deadline behavior without incurring Apify usage.

Requirements
n8n with Data Tables, and the Apify community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify. Tested with: n8n 2.48.2 (Cloud), @apify/n8n-nodes-apify 0.9.0
An Apify account
A Slack workspace where your app may post

Customization
Change the trigger time, the reminder days (remindDaysBefore) or the time zone of the dates (timezone).
Set changeAlerts to deadline to post only moved deadlines and cancellations.
To follow a second market in another copy of the workflow, give that copy's Data Table a different name in its five table nodes.

Additional info
Why it tracks procedures: TED publishes every change to a tender as a new notice with its own number. Of the 42,628 competition notices TED published from 13 October to 12 November 2026, 12,732 (30%) were changes to an earlier notice, and 8,538 of those moved the deadline by a day or more, nearly all of them later, by a median of 7 days. The share of changes differs by country, from 13% to 50% among the ten largest. A monitor keyed on the notice number posts such a tender again as new and keeps counting down to the deadline it saw first.

Limitations: a pause longer than publishedWithinDays misses notices; changing a filter starts a new "Only new notices" history; a tender with lots is one row, and the Actor reports the earliest lot deadline; award notices are not tracked. The table is read in full on every run, so the workflow suits a filtered market (a country, a CPV division), not all of TED. The Code nodes were tested with a day-by-day replay of 12,155 real notices.

Actor used: EU Tenders Scraper on Apify Store — https://kizukidata.com/go/eu-tenders/n8n
Questions or a custom feed: https://kizukidata.com/custom/

workflows.name: Sync phone agent menu and hours with Decodo, Apify, DeepSeek and ElevenLabs
workflows.description:
An AI receptionist works until the lunch price moves or you close early for a holiday. Then it quotes the old menu with confidence, and the caller finds out when the food arrives. Owners in r/restaurantowners and r/smallbusiness say so often. This rebuilds the agent's knowledge each morning from your menu, pricing and FAQ pages plus your Google Business Profile, and touches ElevenLabs only when a price or an hour changed.

Last updated: November 2026.

Quick Overview
Decodo turns each page into markdown and keeps a failed page as a placeholder. Apify reads one Google Places record (name, address, phone, website, hours, rating, review count). DeepSeek V4.1 Flash merges both sides into one document with a fingerprint built from prices and hours, compared against the newest row for that agent. When it changed, the text goes to the ElevenLabs knowledge base, the agent is patched, and you get a voice note, a summary and a spoken preview of today's hours.

How it works
Daily 05:00 or Manual Sync Webhook (POST /sync-agent-knowledge) lands on Config: businessName, agentId, sourceUrls, googleMapsUrl, telegramChatId, voiceId, maxCharsPerPage, timezone, apifyActor.
Split Url List sends each URL to Decodo Scrape Page, a POST to data.decodo.com/v1/scrape for universal markdown, three retries. A failed page passes an empty result.
Trim Page Text keeps 6000 characters and swaps an empty page for "Page could not be loaded, ignore this source.", then Collect Pages builds one array.
Google Places Lookup runs the Apify compass~crawler-google-places actor on googleMapsUrl for one place, no reviews. Keep Safe Place Fields drops the rest.
Merge Sources pairs both lanes by position.
Write Knowledge Doc runs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 0.2 temperature with Knowledge Parser: contact details, hours, parking, menu prices as stated, policies, FAQ, and what it must not promise.
Get Version History reads rows for that agent_id, Only Last Version keeps one, and Knowledge Changed? compares fingerprints. A match ends at No Change Today.
Upload Knowledge Text posts to the Conversational AI knowledge-base endpoint, Attach To Agent PATCHes the agent with the new knowledge_base array, and Save Version stores the fingerprint and doc id.
Narrate Update, Send Update Notice and Narrate Hours Preview run together: a voice note with the change hint, a Telegram summary with the knowledge base id, and a voice note with today's hours.

Setup
Header Auth credential on Decodo Scrape Page with your Web Data API key.
Apify token on Google Places Lookup.
ElevenLabs API key on Upload Knowledge Text, Attach To Agent and both speech nodes.
Put your Conversational AI agent id in agentId. Config ships YOUR_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID, and nothing looks it up for you.
Replace businessName, sourceUrls, googleMapsUrl (your place CID), telegramChatId, voiceId, maxCharsPerPage and timezone.
Create a Data Table agent_knowledge_versions with agent_id, business_name, version_fingerprint, doc_id, changes_hint, version_date and pick it in both Data Table nodes.
Telegram bot credential on the three Telegram nodes and your chat id in Config.
Run the webhook once, read the summary, listen to the hours preview. Everything else is a Config edit.

Quick Answers
What about the agent's other documents?
Attach To Agent sends one item, so the PATCH replaces the whole knowledge_base list. Anything else that agent reads is lost unless you add it there too.

What if a page is down?
The scrape retries three times, then passes an empty result, so that page becomes the placeholder and the document uses the pages that answered. The Telegram notice shows the page count.

Does it rebuild the document every morning?
Only when the fingerprint changes. The Apify call still runs under its 0.5 USD cap, and unchanged prices and hours stop the run at No Change Today.

Can it answer allergen questions?
The document ends with what the agent must not promise, allergens included. DeepSeek still slips, so read a few transcripts in the first week.

Additional info
Built with n8n. Need an assessment on your business? Feel free to reach out at https://khmuhtadin.com/consultation/

workflows.name: Turn permit data into cleaning leads with Decodo, Apify, DeepSeek and ElevenLabs

user.name: Khairul Muhtadin
user.bio: Automation consultant & n8n Ambassador helping teams streamline sales, marketing and operations with AI-powered n8n workflows. Founder of Khaisa Studio and creator of 90+ ready-made n8n templates. Use my link to book a consultation for custom automation work.

workflows.description:
A cleaning company usually hears about a new office build-out weeks after the contractor hired someone. City permit feeds publish tenant improvement filings the day they are issued, while the space is bare and the contract undecided. This workflow reads that feed every weekday morning, matches each build-out to a business on Google Maps, scores the lead, and reads the best ones out loud before your first crew meeting.

Last updated: November 2026.

Quick Overview
Decodo fetches the last seven days of renovation and alteration permits from the feed URL, cost floor and keywords set in Config. Filter Permits keeps the ones above the cost floor that mention commercial space, and Skip Seen Permits drops repeats. Apify Google Maps looks up each address and returns the business name, phone, website and category, and DeepSeek scores the lead 1 to 10 with the likely use, the timing, a first line to say and the contact path. Leads go to a Google Sheet, the best few become a 45 second brief voiced with ElevenLabs, and Telegram and Gmail deliver it.

How it works
Weekday 07:00 runs Monday to Friday at 07:00, and Config builds the permit URL with a seven day window.
Fetch Permits with Decodo posts it to the web data API, Parse Permits reads the JSON, and Split Permits makes one item per permit.
Filter Permits keeps permits at or above minReportedCost whose work description matches a keyword.
Skip Seen Permits drops ids from earlier runs, Any New Permits? routes the rest, and Tell Nothing New answers an empty morning.
Limit Permits caps the batch at maxLeads, and Apify Google Maps searches each address with three results under a $0.50 charge ceiling.
Build Lead keeps the permit fields plus the first Maps match, One Lead Per Permit keeps one row per permit id, and Score Lead sends it to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.
Lead Parser returns lead_score, likely_use, why_now, outreach_line and contact_path. Lead Row shapes the row, Append Lead to Sheet writes it to a Leads tab, and Collect Leads gathers the run.
Write Morning Brief ranks by score and asks DeepSeek for 110 to 130 words. Narrate Brief voices it with ElevenLabs, Send Brief Audio posts the mp3, and Email Lead Table mails the table.

Setup
Add the Decodo key as a Header Auth credential with Authorization: Bearer .
Connect Apify on Apify Google Maps. apifyActor in Config defaults to compass~crawler-google-places.
Connect a DeepSeek credential (OpenAI compatible) on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Brief Model.
Connect ElevenLabs on Narrate Brief and pick the voice. voiceId and eleven_multilingual_v2 sit in Config.
Connect Telegram on Tell Nothing New and Send Brief Audio, and set telegramChatId.
Connect Google Sheets on Append Lead to Sheet, set sheetId, and make a Leads tab with columns runDate, permitId, permitNumber, issueDate, address, communityArea, reportedCost, workDescription, businessName, businessPhone, businessWebsite, businessCategory, mapsRating, mapsReviews, leadScore, likelyUse, whyNow, outreachLine, contactPath.

Does it chase the same permit twice?
Skip Seen Permits remembers permit ids from earlier runs, so each job goes out once.

What happens on a day with no new permits?
Tell Nothing New sends one Telegram line with the date and cost floor; nothing reaches Apify.

How much Apify credit can one morning burn?
maxLeads caps the addresses, each search returns three results, and the run stops at a $0.50 charge.

What if no business shows up at that address?
Build Lead writes "No business found at this address", and the scoring prompt tells the model not to invent one: why_now says the lookup was empty and contact_path points at the site office or the general contractor on the permit. Check a listed phone before calling it a prospect.

workflows.name: Publish reviewed Google Drive images to Facebook and Instagram with Graph API

user.name: Andy
user.bio: I build n8n workflows to make everyday work easier. My templates help automate repetitive tasks and come with clear instructions and examples so you can get started.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Publish exact reviewed Drive images through controlled Facebook and Instagram adapters. Match private and public JPEG bytes, approve caption, accounts and UTC timing, recheck before each send, preserve original IDs and stop ambiguous retries. Dry run is the default.

How it works
Reads a dedicated Google Sheets queue and one initialized native Data Table pipeline. Validates unique job IDs, explicit rights/public-hosting flags, allowed account IDs and a valid future UTC schedule with an IANA timezone display.
Reads private Drive metadata and the actual JPEG, verifies the configured parent folder and version, and compares its SHA-256 with the customer-owned immutable public JPEG mirror.
Requires an allowlisted signed-in n8n reviewer to inspect the actual source and approve the exact content hash, state version, caption, target accounts and UTC time. Dry-run approval is distinct from permission to publish.
In dry run, rechecks the source and emits a request manifest without a Meta publishing call. Dry-run approval never enables live publication.
Only in explicitly enabled live mode, verifies the Facebook Page or linked professional Instagram identity, rechecks the image and persists a send-ready intent before each mutation.
Uses Graph v26.0 Facebook photo publication and Instagram image container/status/media_publish adapters. Instagram may prepare its unpublished container shortly before due; public publication waits for the approved UTC window.
Stores each original channel ID, then verifies account ownership, caption and provider permalink. A successful channel is not reposted when the other fails.
Ambiguous provider responses stop the job for explicit original-ID reconciliation; the Google Sheets queue mirrors authoritative Data Table status.

Setup
Import setup.json, workflow.json and review.json into a compatible n8n project and keep them inactive. Connect Google Sheets OAuth and run the one-time resource creator for a new PublishQueue and initialized native Data Table.
Copy the reported spreadsheet/table IDs and your own private My Drive source folder into both configurations. Set exact public-media hostnames, numeric Facebook/Instagram account allowlists, the linked Instagram Page map and real reviewer emails.
Supply an exact-byte immutable publicly reachable HTTPS JPEG mirror; a private Drive/viewer URL is not valid hosting. This package does not upload public copies or change sharing permissions.
Connect Google Drive OAuth and separate native Meta Authorization Bearer Header Auth credentials. Obtain your own eligible Meta app, Facebook Page/professional Instagram accounts, appropriate permissions and Page access tokens using the Facebook Login route.
Run the credential-free synthetic demo, then a real-source dry run. Only after your own controlled live account test and explicit authorization should you create a new live job policy, set dryRun=false, enable publishing and approve exact public publication. Keep the minute worker running for due schedules.

Requirements
Compatible n8n 2.28.6-style native Data Tables, Form Trigger2.6/n8n User Auth and Completion2.5; Google Sheets/Drive OAuth and a private My Drive input folder; exact-byte immutable public HTTPS JPEG hosting; suitable Facebook Page and linked professional Instagram account where used; Meta app, current publishing grants and appropriate Page access tokens; real allowlisted reviewer accounts. V1 accepts single JPEGs within the documented size/dimension policy. No Meta account, token, public hosting or app-review approval is supplied. Only local/pure and strict isolated mock tests were performed; real account eligibility, real posts, Google delivery and Cloud are untested.

Customization
Configure exact accounts, linked Page mapping, trusted CDN hosts, UTC schedules, IANA display zones, poll and lateness limits, and reviewers. The approved policy includes dry-run mode; changing it cannot turn an old dry-run approval into live permission. Keep fresh private/public byte checks, authenticated exact-version review, per-channel original IDs and persisted send gates intact. Use a new unique job for changed source/caption/targets/time, and target only unresolved channels after independently resolving any uncertain original publication.

Additional info
Includes inactive worker, authenticated review companion, setup and a credential-free synthetic demo. Local fixtures and isolated native mocks cover adapter requests, original-ID reconciliation and repeat handling; real Meta posts, real Google delivery, account eligibility and n8n Cloud were not live-tested. Dry run makes no Meta requests. Public JPEG hosting must remain immutable while Meta fetches it. No video, Reel, Story, carousel, automatic hosting, provider-side scheduling, remote deletion or guaranteed exactly-once/exact-time publication is included.

Quick overview
This workflow runs every weekday morning and calls an Apify actor to fetch newly published German construction tenders that include GAEB bill-of-quantities positions, then formats each tender into a readable summary with keyword hit snippets for downstream use.

How it works
Runs at 07:00 (Europe/Berlin) every Monday to Friday.
Sends a POST request to the Apify API to run the “german-construction-tenders-gaeb” actor synchronously with filters such as publication window, CPV prefixes, keywords, GAEB-only, and maximum tender count.
Parses the returned dataset items and, for each tender, extracts key fields like buyer, submission deadline, location, GAEB position count, and documents URL.
Matches keyword hits against GAEB positions and generates short text excerpts/snippets around the first matched keyword to provide context.
Outputs one formatted item per tender, including a prebuilt multi-line message summarizing the tender and up to five keyword-hit positions.

Setup
Create an Apify account, get an API token, and replace YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN in the Apify request URL (or store it as an n8n HTTP Query Auth credential parameter named token).
Adjust the Apify request JSON body to set your desired filters (for example keywords, cpvPrefixes, pubDaysBack, and maxTenders).
(Optional) Add region filters like postalCodePrefixes or nutsPrefixes to the Apify request body to narrow results and keep the sync run within the timeout.

Requirements
An Apify account and API token for the German Construction Tenders + GAEB Extractor (https://apify.com/brsksr/german-construction-tenders-gaeb). No German procurement portal accounts or logins are required.

Customization
Filter by specific German postal code prefixes (postalCodePrefixes, e.g., ["10", "80"]), NUTS regions (nutsPrefixes), or custom product keywords inside GAEB .x83, .d83, and .p83 Bills of Quantities.

Additional info
Covers ~85% of public German construction notices via oeffentlichevergabe.de, including Cosinex, subreport ELViS, evergabe.de, Deutsche eVergabe, evergabe-online.de, AI NetServer (HAD, Hessen, BW), and Healy Hudson (Deutsche Bahn, Hamburg).

workflows.name: Track LLM spend per workflow and send budget alerts via the n8n API

user.name: Le Thua Phu
user.bio: I'm passionate about leveraging n8n to create seamless workflows that blend AI capabilities with data automation. Based in Vietnam, I specialize in building efficient, scalable solutions to streamline business processes and unlock the power of data. workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every 15 minutes, reads recent n8n executions via the n8n API, extracts LLM token usage from AI and HTTP Request nodes, logs per-call cost into an n8n Data Table, and sends Slack/email/Telegram/webhook alerts for budget overruns, spend spikes, loops, and unpriced models.

How it works
Runs every 15 minutes on a schedule.
Calls the n8n Public API to fetch execution data since the last saved checkpoint.
Extracts LLM calls from execution run data (chat model sub-nodes and raw provider responses from nodes like OpenAI/Anthropic/Google Gemini and HTTP Request), calculates token totals, and estimates USD cost from the configured per-model pricing.
Writes only new LLM-call rows into an n8n Data Table using a unique call key to deduplicate across runs.
Reads the last 8 days of logged usage and analyzes today’s spend per workflow to detect budget overruns, spikes versus the prior 7-day daily average, excessive calls per execution (loops), and models missing a price.
Optionally unpublishes over-budget workflows when configured, then routes each alert to Slack, SMTP email, Telegram, or a custom webhook.

Setup
Create an n8n API key and add an n8n API credential, then set your n8n base URL and select the credential for fetching executions and (optionally) unpublishing workflows.
Create an n8n Data Table with the required columns (callKey, execution/workflow metadata, token counts, costUsd, estimated, finishedAt) and select it in all Data Table steps.
Update the configuration values for model pricing, daily budgets/overrides, spike/loop thresholds, and whether to unpublish over-budget workflows.
Choose an alert channel and configure only the matching integration credential (Slack, SMTP, or Telegram) plus destination values (Slack channel, alert email, or Telegram chat ID), or enable and set the webhook URL for webhook alerts.
Execute the workflow once and then publish it so the checkpoint and once-per-day alert suppression are persisted across runs.

Requirements
n8n instance with the public API and Data tables (self-hosted, or a Cloud plan with API access)
n8n API key
Credential for your alert channel: Slack, SMTP, Telegram bot, or none for a webhook
Workflows to monitor must keep their execution data

Customization
Change the 15 minute interval in Every 15 minutes
Update pricesPer1M when providers change prices or you add models
Set per-workflow budgets with budgetOverrides, for example {"workflowId": 20}
Tune maxCallsPerExecution, spikeMultiplier and spikeMinUsd to match your usage
Set pauseOverBudget to true to unpublish a workflow that goes over budget
Add another alert node to the Route alert by channel Switch node

Additional info
Use cases: finding which workflow, node and model spends the most tokens, and catching a looping agent before it burns your budget. Output: one data table row per LLM call, with workflow, node, model, tokens and cost in USD. Limits: the first run reads only the latest 50 executions, each run reads at most 1,000 new executions, and executions waiting in a Wait node are skipped. Calls from HTTP Request and standalone AI nodes are counted only when the node output keeps the provider usage or usageMetadata field. The prices in pricesPer1M are examples, so check your provider pricing pages. Alerts are sent once per day per alert, and this memory is saved only when the workflow is published.

workflows.name: Create Instagram and Facebook carousels from articles with Claude, OpenAI and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow takes an article URL and market selection from an n8n form, uses Anthropic Claude to draft carousel copy and OpenAI to generate images, builds branded assets in Cloudinary, then requests Slack approval before publishing an Instagram carousel and story + Facebook Page post via the Meta Graph API.

How it works
An editor submits an n8n form with a published article URL and a target market.
The workflow loads market-specific brand settings, checks the carousel_posts data table for prior posts of the same article, and shows a “generation started” confirmation.
It fetches the article HTML, extracts the title, body text, and a hero image URL, then asks Anthropic Claude to generate three slide texts, three image prompts, and a caption.
It validates the generated text and prompts (for example, blocking Title Case headlines and unsafe colour cues in warning-related image prompts) before generating any paid images.
It downloads the hero image, generates slide and story images with OpenAI Images, uploads assets to Cloudinary, and composes four carousel slides plus a story using Cloudinary transformations.
It bakes the transformed images into flat Cloudinary assets, posts a preview to Slack, and waits up to three hours for an approval or a “More options” review decision.
If approved and accounts are configured, it publishes the carousel to Instagram and Facebook and publishes an Instagram story, then logs post IDs and metadata back to the carousel_posts data table.
If “More options” is selected, it lets the reviewer rewrite the cover headline with Claude or regenerate one image with OpenAI and re-posts updated previews to Slack, or declines without publishing.

Logs each scored post to an n8n Data Table and optionally appends the same data to a Google Sheets tab.

workflows.name: Monitor SPF, DKIM and DMARC across multiple domains with Apify, Gmail and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily (or on demand) to audit SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for multiple domains using the Apify Email Deliverability Auditor, tracks changes in an n8n Data Table ledger, and notifies results via Gmail digest emails and Slack messages for new, changed, or fixed findings.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule at 7:00 or is started manually, then loads domain, DKIM selector, and notification settings from a configuration block.
Ensures a deliverability_ledger n8n Data Table exists and splits the configured domain list into one item per domain.
Calls the Apify Email Deliverability Auditor Actor for each domain to check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, retrying once after 30 seconds if the audit fails.
Converts each audit result into per-check findings (critical, warning, info, or ok), including a recorded DNS/audit failure finding when both attempts fail.
Compares the current findings to the Data Table ledger to label each check as new, changed, still open, fixed, or ok, then upserts the latest state back to the ledger.
Builds an HTML digest and a Slack change summary, then sends the digest via Gmail every run and posts to Slack only when there are changes.

Setup
Add an Apify HTTP Header Auth credential with an Authorization header set to Bearer .
Connect Gmail credentials for sending the digest email and Slack credentials for posting messages (or disable either channel in the configuration).
Update the CONFIG block with your domains, DKIM selectors, notification email address, and Slack channel name.
Ensure your n8n instance supports Data Tables and that it can create/use a table named deliverability_ledger.

Requirements
n8n with Data Tables (tested on 2.43), an Apify account (Email Deliverability Auditor Actor), Gmail and/or Slack.

Customization
Tune spfLookupWarningAt, dmarcTargetPolicy, softfailIsInfo and requireDkim in CONFIG. About $0.002 per domain per check on Apify.

Additional info

workflows.name: Create and approve WordPress articles and social videos with Airtable, OpenAI, Tavily, Gmail, Facebook and Instagram

user.name: Matilda Ivy
user.bio:
I’m interested in what happens between a good automation idea and a system that actually works.

I enjoy the problem-solving side: tracing failures, figuring out why things behave unexpectedly, and getting the whole system working.

I share practical workflows and what I learn while building them.

M-Automations | m-automations.com

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow checks Airtable for due content topics, researches them with Tavily, generates and edits an article plus images and a short video using OpenAI, then waits for Gmail approval before publishing to WordPress, Facebook, and Instagram and writing all asset links back to Airtable.

How it works
Runs on a schedule or manually and selects one Airtable record marked Ready whose Planned Date is due.
Uses Tavily to gather sources, then OpenAI to draft an article and review its claims against the retrieved research.
Generates an SEO title, category, meta description, slug and FAQs, then converts the article and FAQs into HTML.
Creates a feature-image brief and prompt, generates the feature image and five article-based slide illustrations with native OpenAI image nodes, and uploads the images to Cloudinary and ImageKit.
Selects a music track from Google Sheets, checks its ID against an n8n Data Table, retries used tracks, and downloads the selected audio from Google Drive.
Uses FFmpeg to combine the five illustrations, captions and background music into a vertical video, uploads it to ImageKit, and automatically removes temporary rendering files.
Generates social captions, marks the record Awaiting approval, and sends the article, captions and media links to a reviewer through Gmail.
Approval publishes to WordPress, Facebook and Instagram, including an Instagram Reel, then records assets and published links in Airtable with Status set to Published. Rejection marks Needs changes and stops without publishing.

Setup
Connect Airtable credentials and select your base/table in the Airtable nodes. Create Topic, Content Brief, Planned Date and Status fields, plus the output fields listed in the workflow notes. Add Ready, Awaiting approval, Needs changes and Published status options.
Configure Tavily Header Auth credentials and OpenAI credentials. Select the text and image models in their respective nodes.
Configure Cloudinary and ImageKit credentials, account settings and upload presets. Uploaded media must have direct URLs accessible to the publishing platforms.
Connect Google Sheets and Google Drive, select your music spreadsheet, and configure the Used Music Ids Data Table. Keep the music_id, title and artist_name library columns.
Install FFmpeg, ffprobe and a suitable font in the environment executing the video Code node. Permit the fs and child_process modules, and adjust the font path in Build Captioned Video.
Connect Gmail credentials and enter the reviewer’s email in Review Content Before Publishing. Ensure your public n8n approval links are reachable.
Configure WordPress Application Password authentication and your site URL. Connect Meta credentials and replace the Facebook Page and Instagram account placeholders with accounts that have the required publishing permissions.

Requirements
Self-hosted n8n with FFmpeg, ffprobe, an installed font and task-runner access to fs and child_process.
Airtable, Tavily and OpenAI credentials.
Google Sheets and Google Drive access for the music library, plus an n8n Data Table for used track IDs.
Cloudinary and ImageKit accounts for the included storage steps.
Gmail credentials and a reviewer email address.
WordPress REST API access, a Facebook Page and an Instagram professional account with appropriate publishing permissions.
Music you have permission to publish.

Customization
Adjust topics, content briefs, writing prompts and the production schedule.
Replace text or image providers by adapting their output mappings.
Replace Cloudinary or ImageKit with your preferred storage. Google Drive can be used if you provide directly fetchable media URLs; ordinary sharing-page links are insufficient.
Adjust video captions, font, scene duration and music volume.
Use your own music library and approval recipient.

Additional info
Human approval is required before any WordPress, Facebook or Instagram publishing.
Videos use captions and library music; no narration service is required.
Rejected topics are marked Needs changes. Edit the brief and return the topic to Ready to regenerate.
Approved assets and published links are saved to the same Airtable record.
Temporary rendering files are automatically deleted.
Use one generation at a time. Inspect any already-published posts before retrying a partially completed publishing run.
Connected-service charges depend on usage.

user.name: Retailbox Automation
user.bio: RetailBox Automation builds n8n and AI automations for growing businesses. In business since 2019, based in Orlando, FL. Top Rated Plus on Upwork with 477 jobs and 100% Job Success. If you need a workflow built or fixed, book a call through the link.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every 15 minutes, pulls recent n8n executions via the n8n API, calculates per-call LLM token costs, stores them in an n8n Data Table, and posts a Slack alert when any workflow exceeds its daily budget (optionally deactivating the workflow).

How it works
Runs every 15 minutes on a schedule.
Retrieves the latest active-workflow executions (including execution details) from the n8n API.
Extracts each chat model call from the execution run data, reads stored token usage (or estimates), matches the model to a price list, and calculates a USD cost per call.
Checks an n8n Data Table to skip LLM calls that have already been logged, then inserts only new usage rows.
Reads today’s rows from the Data Table, totals spend per workflow, and identifies workflows that exceed their configured daily budget while ensuring only one alert per workflow per day.
Optionally deactivates over-budget workflows via the n8n API, then sends a budget-overrun message to a Slack channel.

Setup
Create an n8n API key and add an n8n API credential, then select it in the n8n nodes used to list executions and deactivate workflows.
Create an n8n Data Table with the required columns (including callKey, workflowId, token counts, costUsd, and finishedAt) and select the table in all Data Table nodes.
Connect a Slack credential and choose the target channel for alerts.
Update the configuration values for pricesPer1M, dailyBudgetUsd, budgetOverrides, and pauseOverBudget to match your models, budgets, and desired behavior.

Requirements
n8n API access (self-hosted, or a Cloud plan that includes the API), Data tables, Slack.

Customization
Change the interval, raise Limit in Get recent executions if you run more than 100 executions per interval, or send the alert by email instead of Slack.

Additional info
A row is marked estimated when the provider returned no usage and n8n stored its own estimate. On n8n 2.43 the OpenAI Chat Model node with Use Responses API switched on stores only the estimate. Switch it off for exact counts.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors SSL certificate expiry and security headers for a list of websites using Apify, stores the last known state in an n8n Data Table, and sends change-based alerts and a weekly summary to Slack, Gmail, and an optional webhook.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule, on demand, or on Mondays for the weekly summary, and loads the site list and notification settings from the CONFIG block.
Creates (if needed) and reads the ssl_monitor_state n8n Data Table to keep track of each site’s last known grade, certificate status, and open issues.
On daily/manual runs, calls the Apify “Security Headers & SSL Audit” Actor to audit each site’s HTTPS/certificate status, redirects, and security headers.
Compares the latest audit results with the stored state to detect new, changed, reminder-due, and resolved issues, with “site unreachable” only alerting after consecutive failed checks.
Saves the updated per-site state back to the ssl_monitor_state Data Table and builds a single consolidated alert message when any changes are detected.
Routes alerts by severity and sends them to the enabled channels via Slack, Gmail, and/or an HTTP webhook, retrying sends without blocking other channels.
On weekly summary runs, generates a summary from the stored state (without running Apify) and sends it through the same notification channels.

Setup
Create an Apify account and add an HTTP Header Auth credential with Authorization: Bearer  for the Apify request.
Add Slack credentials and set the target channel in CONFIG if you want Slack notifications.
Add Gmail credentials and set the recipient address and minimum severity in CONFIG if you want email notifications.
If using a webhook (for example Discord or Microsoft Teams), enable it in CONFIG and paste the webhook URL.
Update CONFIG with your site domains, certificate warning/critical thresholds, minimum headers grade, and reminder/consecutive-failure settings before activating the workflow.

Requirements
n8n with Data Tables (tested on 2.43), an Apify account (
Security Headers & SSL Audit Actor) and Slack and/or Gmail.

Customization
criticalReminderDays, email.minSeverity and confirmUnreachableChecks. Set previewWeeklySummary to true to test the summary. About $0.003 per site per check on Apify.
